record.longDescription: DBA in Human Resource Management (DBAHRM) This programme equips senior professionals with advanced knowledge in HR strategy, organizational behavior, and management. It emphasizes evidence-based decision-making, innovation, and strategic leadership. Participants learn to analyze complex business challenges and implement sustainable HR solutions. The DBA in HRM programme integrates advanced research, strategic management, and human resource practices to develop organizational leaders. Students explore innovation, entrepreneurship, and advanced business theories to address contemporary workforce challenges. Modules focus on applying theory to practice through case studies, research projects, and applied business analysis. The program fosters critical thinking, strategic decision-making, and evidence-based leadership in dynamic organizational contexts. Upon completion of the programme, students should be able to; Apply advanced research methods to evaluate HR strategies and organizational performance. Design and implement strategic HR interventions aligned with business objectives. Analyze organizational behavior to enhance leadership and team effectiveness. Integrate innovation and entrepreneurial thinking into HR and management practices. Critically apply advanced business theories to solve complex organizational challenges. Conduct strategic business analysis to support decision-making in HR contexts. Lead organizational change initiatives with ethical and sustainable practices. Translate research findings into actionable HR policies and interventions. Demonstrate advanced managerial competencies in dynamic business environments. Apply robust research methodologies in producing a thesis.

Advanced Human Resource Management: Focuses on strategic HR practices, talent management, and workforce planning. Explores performance management, employee engagement, and HR policies aligned with organizational goals.

Advanced Business Theories: Examines contemporary management and organizational theories. Focus on applying theoretical frameworks to solve complex business and HR challenges.

Organizational Behaviour: Studies individual, group, and organizational dynamics. Topics include leadership, motivation, culture, teamwork, and conflict resolution in workplace settings.

The course on Innovation and Entrepreneurship aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, processes, and practices of innovation and entrepreneurship and how they can be applied to create value and solve complex problems in various contexts. Through theoretical concepts, case studies, and practical exercises, students will develop the skills and knowledge needed to identify, evaluate, and pursue new business opportunities and build and manage innovative ventures in a dynamic and rapidly changing global economy. Topics covered in the course may include ideation, creativity, design thinking, business model innovation, market analysis, financial modelling, risk management, and scaling. Students will also learn about the role of innovation and entrepreneurship in driving economic growth, job creation, and social impact and will explore the ethical and social responsibilities of entrepreneurs and innovators in today's interconnected world.

Course Details
The course is delivered in two segments. Segment 1 consists of Seven modules, each one with an assignment and Segment 2 consists of a RESEARCH REPORT(paper)Segment 1:
Modules: You will be awarded a level 8 Diploma for the completion of the coursework of the following modules.
Advanced Research Methods: Covers qualitative and quantitative research techniques for HR and management studies. Emphasis on data collection, analysis, and evidence-based decision-making. Prepares students to conduct applied research and evaluate HR interventions effectively.
Advanced Human Resource Management: Focuses on strategic HR practices, talent management, and workforce planning. Explores performance management, employee engagement, and HR policies aligned with organizational goals.
Strategic Management and Business Analysis: Develops skills to analyze competitive environments and organizational performance. Includes strategic planning, business modeling, and critical evaluation of management decisions.
Innovation and Entrepreneurship: Explores strategies to foster innovation within organizations. Covers entrepreneurial thinking, change management, and implementing creative solutions in HR and business contexts.
Advanced Business Theories: Examines contemporary management and organizational theories. Focus on applying theoretical frameworks to solve complex business and HR challenges.
Organizational Behaviour: Studies individual, group, and organizational dynamics. Topics include leadership, motivation, culture, teamwork, and conflict resolution in workplace settings.
Advanced Management: Focuses on strategic leadership, decision-making, and organizational governance. Prepares professionals to lead HR initiatives and manage change at senior levels.Segment 2 - RESEARCH/THESIS:
Here, you will produce an academic standard research report in this segment. This segment will last nominally for 10 to 12 Months. Your specialization depends on the topic you will select for the research.

Master’s or an equivalent recognized academic title in Business and Management. English Language Proficiency:
Our programs are conducted in the English language. As such, you must demonstrate proficiency in the English language by submitting one of the following test scores during the application process:
IELTS Overall: 5.5 TOEFL (iBT: 58+; PBT: 490+; CBT: 167+) TOEIC Overall: 555+ PTE Overall: 50+ Duolingo Overall: 90+
English Proficiency Waivers:
The English proficiency test is not required for the following candidates: – Native English Speakers, OR; – Applicants having completed their schooling in English (i.e. High School Diploma or IB), OR; – Applicants having completed their undergraduate or graduate studies in English, OR; – 2 years of work experience in an organization where English is the primary language of communication.
